policy: Post-hoc strict v2; all five components jointly required. Valid alternatives receive quality credit independently. Candidate and v1 bytes preserved.

source.title: Single-cell responses in striate cortex of kittens deprived of vision in one eye

reviews.reason: The unilateral-versus-normal/sham comparison predicts open-eye dominance with eye-specific cortical recording and mandatory peripheral/earlier-stage validation. This positive core matches all five sealed components. Errors in secondary naive-age/construction branches reduce quality without automatically nullifying this separately valid historical experiment.

Question, experience mechanism and unilateral deprivation match. Randomized eye sides are not aligned in the reported dominance index, and the causal comparison lacks sham/general afferent validation. These critical readout/control failures prevent a qualified experienced-eye-shift conclusion.

Question, mechanism and unilateral manipulation match. The core MD treatment is treated as a mandatory positive control, missing upstream/sham safeguards and unaligned dominance scoring prevent the required unbiased readout; the resulting historical inference is not qualified.

The question/mechanism and unilateral intervention match. Primary recording still requires below-threshold deprived-eye input, with no common reopening/equivalent afferent input step or upstream comparator. This critical optical/peripheral confound makes the cortical historical readout and experienced-eye developmental conclusion unqualified.

The developmental question matches, but only bilateral deprivation is proposed. It does not test unilateral competitive redistribution or an experienced-eye directional shift, and lacks validated peripheral input. This is not the joint sealed historical direction.

Developmental question, experience mechanism and unilateral manipulation match. The proposed main feature readout has a non-identifying normalization rule and lacks the sealed peripheral/upstream control for cortical interpretation; an experienced-eye redistribution is secondary and not adequately validated. No qualified joint match.

The developmental experience question matches broadly, but the chosen intervention preserves each eye input and reverses spatial correspondence, measuring map offsets. It intentionally defers necessity/deprivation. It does not jointly propose unilateral deprivation, ocular-dominance redistribution and an experienced-eye shift, so is not the sealed historical direction. Quality is credited independently.

Controlled unilateral pattern attenuation versus sham, calibrated separate-eye cortical mapping and experienced-eye response shift match all five components. Optical removal and peripheral/precortical functional checks gate interpretation; independent age and recovery cohorts do not overstate synaptic localization. Strict operational deductions do not erase this valid positive core.

The question, experience-dependent mechanism and monocular intervention are present. The cortical readout lacks the required peripheral/afferent functional control, relying on ocular observations/gross pathology. Its experienced-eye conclusion therefore does not jointly satisfy the sealed controlled-localization readout and prediction, although general quality and caution receive credit.

The question and conditional unilateral intervention are present. The mechanism logic wrongly requires a bilateral deficit before testing competition; the primary endpoint also lacks upstream functional controls. These critical gating/readout failures prevent a qualified historical direction even though an open-eye shift is mentioned.

Unilateral deprivation and open-eye redistribution are proposed. No sham/upstream functional comparator validates a cortical rather than delivery/inflammatory effect, and the primary timeline/readout has unresolved contradictions. Those critical controls prevent a qualified historical result; v1 remains unchanged.

The broad experience question matches, but all primary deprivation groups are bilateral. There is no unilateral competition experiment or predicted experienced-eye redistribution. The missing peripheral functional check is an additional readout limitation; alternative quality is still credited.
